FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox test execution correctly when a `test_cmd` references source files outside the tempdir. In `bench/endocrine.py`, the patched file is written only as `tmpdir/basename.py`, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged with `cwd=tmpdir`. The default integration path from `immune_agents.py` passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`, which resolves relative to the tempdir and therefore targets a non-existent `bench/tests/` tree. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` copies only one file, does not copy the repo or rewrite `test_cmd`, then runs `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`.
FOLLOW: This makes the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” capability largely non-functional in the actual integration path. Downstream, fix evaluations will frequently mark `tests_passed=False` due to path failure rather than code breakage, driving `_compute_fix_verdict()` to return `HARMFUL`. In the immune pipeline, Stage 4 uses `evaluate_fixes()` to set `finding.verified=True` only for SAFE/NEUTRAL fixes; false HARMFUL verdicts therefore suppress verification, keep bugs from closing, and prevent the NK bug-closed gate from firing on later rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — before running tests, copy the repository subtree needed by the test command into the tempdir and write the patched file at its original relative path inside that copied tree; then run `test_cmd` against that mirrored tree from the tempdir. Simplest sufficient variant: copy the project root containing the target file and `bench/tests/`, patch the mirrored target file in place, then execute the unchanged test command with `cwd` set to the mirrored project root.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` can report a source-modifying fix as SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL even when the patched file cannot be imported by the code that depends on its package context, because the sandbox strips package structure. It writes the patched file to `tmpdir/os.path.basename(target_path)` and runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that orphan file. For files that rely on package-relative imports or neighboring modules, diagnostics on the orphaned file are not equivalent to diagnostics in situ.
FOLLOW: This breaks the core promise that fix evaluation measures whether a proposed change is safe for the real codebase. Downstream consequences cross the immune interface: Stage 4 in `immune_agents.py` may mark a fix `verified=True` from an orphan-file analysis even though the same file would fail when evaluated at its real path within the package. That creates silently wrong “verified fix” state, enabling the NK bug-closed gate to close future reports on a bug whose fix was never actually validated in the real module context.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — preserve the original relative path inside the sandbox instead of flattening to basename. Copy the minimal package tree containing the target file into the tempdir, patch the mirrored file at the same relative path, and run tool checks against that mirrored path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses a summed net-change score (`net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`) so regressions in one tool can be cancelled out by improvements in another. Example from the implemented logic: a fix that removes two ruff warnings but introduces one new pyright error yields total_net = -1 and is classified SAFE. That is silently wrong for fix validation because a new type error is still a regression.
FOLLOW: The downstream effect is false SAFE verdicts for harmful fixes. Through the immune pipeline integration, Stage 4 treats SAFE/NEUTRAL as programmatically verified and sets `finding.verified=True`. That can close a bug based on a fix that actually introduced a new correctness or security issue, and later NK dedup will suppress rediscovery as “bug closed.” This is a high-severity silent-wrong-result path.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta as HARMFUL before considering aggregate improvement. Concretely: if `net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`, return `HARMFUL`; otherwise keep the existing SAFE/NEUTRAL logic for zero-or-negative deltas.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_pyright()` records pyright positions without converting from pyright’s 0-based coordinates to the 1-based line numbering used elsewhere in the module (`run_mypy`, `run_bandit`, `run_ruff`) and expected by humans. It stores `rng.get("line", 0)` and `rng.get("character", 0)` directly. Pyright JSON positions are 0-based.
FOLLOW: This yields inconsistent diagnostic coordinates inside a single `HealthScan`: pyright findings point one line earlier than mypy/ruff/bandit. Downstream, `counts_by_file` still works, but any consumer that surfaces line numbers for reviewer action or tries to correlate endocrine diagnostics with findings from the immune/brain layers will mislocate pyright issues. That is a silently misleading output in the health monitor.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — add 1 to pyright line and column values when constructing `ToolDiagnostic`, while keeping 0 only for truly unknown coordinates.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43
DESCRIPTION: FIND — CrossHair is declared as a supported tool and given a binary path/timeout, but it is never run anywhere in endocrine.py. The module docstring, `ToolDiagnostic.tool` comment, and binary constants all advertise CrossHair-backed health/fix checking, yet `scan_health()` invokes only pyright, ruff, bandit, and mypy, and fix evaluation never calls CrossHair either.
FOLLOW: This is dead capability in a module whose job is to produce mechanical health signals. Downstream, reviewers and orchestrator logic can believe symbolic execution coverage exists when it does not. Because the endocrine layer is supposed to close blind spots between rounds, the missing tool reduces actual defect-detection coverage while overstating it in the interface.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove CrossHair from the advertised endocrine interface for now: delete the unused binary constant/docs mentions or mark it explicitly unimplemented. Simplest sufficient PoC fix is to stop claiming CrossHair support until a runner exists.
VERIFIED: TRUE
